messages:
Sam (runtime): heads-up: seeing a sudden tail-latency spike on prod pool-5 starting ~09:12 UTC. p50 unchanged, p95 ~120ms -> 320ms, p99 ~90ms -> 480ms. throughput steady. Noticed a concurrent bump in KV cache evictions.
Maria (kernel): thanks. any runaway kernel selector changes rolled recently?
Sam (runtime): not on prod config; we did push a candidate yesterday to canary that tweaks kernel preference weights for grouped-attn -> fused-attn for some llama variants. Deploy-bot noted that canary passed, but prod stayed on prior.
Rahul (scheduler): scheduler telemetry shows an increase in microbatch fragmentation — more 1-token microbatches being admitted around the same time. admission rate oscillating between 140 and 220 reqs/s on that pool.
Jules (profiling): attaching quick flame excerpt:
```
# flame top (shortened)
KVCache::evict (30%)
Scheduler::admit (18%)
KernelSelector::choose_kernel (14%)
Microbatch::build (10%)
GPUTask::execute (18%)
```
Notably KVCache::evict jumped before KernelSelector's hot path.
Lia (oncall): what about noisy tenants? any tenant bursting?
Sam (runtime): tenant-side metrics: one tenant had a short burst of many short requests (mostly short-chat completions). Their median tokens/request ~6. TTL for KV prefix match low; combined with fragmented microbatches looks like we thrash the KV shards.
Maria (kernel): if eviction increases, our kernel selector sometimes falls back to a lower-memory kernel to avoid OOMs, which is slower for short sequences. That would explain p99 jump while p50 stays fine.
Rahul (scheduler): hypothesis: burst of tiny requests -> more microbatches with high headroom -> admission controller ramps admit window down to avoid queue depth, triggers fragmentation. Combined with KV eviction fanout causes kernel selector to see degraded memory headroom and switch kernels.
Jules (profiling): I ran a quick perf on a repro cluster: with KV eviction enabled at that rate, fused-attn kernel latency increases 2.7x for seq<=16. Swapping to the fallback kernel adds 1.8x.
Sam (runtime): immediate mitigation: throttled the noisy tenant at 09:30 UTC (rate-limit rule), ramped KV cache watermark up slightly to reduce eviction frequency, and pinned kernel selector to prefer fused-attn on pool-5 to prevent fallback.
Infra-bot: action taken: rate-limit-rule applied to tenant xyz-123, KVCache watermark increased by 10%, kernel-select override applied to pool-5.
Lia (oncall): after mitigations: p99 down to ~140ms within 8m, p95 ~90ms. No further oscillation in admission rate.
Maria (kernel): long-term fixes to consider: 1) make kernel selector aware of transient KV eviction signals and delay fallback for short seqs, 2) add per-tenant admission shaping to avoid single-tenant fanout, 3) improve KV shard hotness isolation.
Rahul (scheduler): also want to add microbatch coalescing for short requests — if many 1-3 token requests arrive within X ms, temporarily prefer batch packing instead of immediate admission to reduce microbatch overhead.
Jules (profiling): I'll open a profiling runbook entry with the flame outputs and script to reproduce with synthetic short-request traffic + KV eviction toggles.
Sam (runtime): opened follow-ups:
- sam/eviction-kernel-investigation (RFC) -> propose selector hysteresis for eviction events
- rahul/coalesce-short-batches (spike) -> prototype microbatch coalescer with 5ms window
- jules/repro-scripts (artifact) -> reproducer and perf logs

Sam (runtime): TL;DR: root cause is interaction between KVCache eviction fanout + scheduler microbatch fragmentation causing kernel selector to fallback. Mitigated by rate-limit + watermark + selector override. Tracking longer-term: selector hysteresis + batch coalescing + KV hot-tenant isolation. :thumbsup:
